delivery_path: branch -> pull request -> CI checks -> reviewed merge -> deploy
definition_of_ready: Target school role, user problem, and success metric are named.
Primary critical user journey and failure-sensitive points are documented or explicitly referenced.
Affected routes, Prisma models, auth roles, middleware paths, Docker or CI surfaces, and deploy surfaces are identified.
Release-risky boundaries from .jarvis/production_grade_profile.json#architecture are named when auth, Prisma, middleware, Docker, CI, or deploy behavior may change.
Required verification commands are selected from verification_contract.json before implementation starts.
Rollback or release-abort condition is explicit before broad implementation starts.
definition_of_done: Behavior changes are covered by focused tests or documented as intentionally unchanged.
The selected verification gates pass, or blocked gates and residual risk are recorded in .codex/reports/release-readiness.md.
Product-facing pull requests name the target role, critical user journey, success metric, verification evidence, and rollback or abort condition.
Deploy-facing changes include /health smoke evidence, restart or rollout evidence where applicable, and rollback notes.
No secrets, .env files, database dumps, generated build artifacts, or real student/family data are committed.
The pull request remains small enough to review and can be reverted without unrelated behavior changes.

risk_classification.low: Documentation, advisory config, contract tests, and release evidence with no runtime behavior change.
risk_classification.medium: Application behavior or dependency changes that preserve schema, auth, middleware, and deploy contracts.
risk_classification.high: Auth, Prisma schema or migration, middleware, Docker, CI, deployment, data access, or role-routing changes.

blocked_work_policy: Do not broaden implementation when Definition of Ready is not met. Record the blocker, owner gap, or missing evidence in .codex/reports/release-readiness.md and split the work into a smaller ready item.

rollback.primary: Revert the pull request or redeploy previous_release.
rollback.database: Use backward-compatible Prisma migrations; do not run destructive database rollback without a tested restore plan.
